paragraphs.source_en: The king, it seems, still had a lingering desire for them, and asked how much she would take for the three volumes; the woman, they say, still demanded the price of all nine. Nine volumes had become six, and six had become three, yet the price remained exactly as before; she would not reduce it by a single penny. If he pressed her to lower it, she might well throw the remaining three volumes into the fire too, so at last the king paid the extravagant sum and bought the three that had escaped the flames. My husband said to me, 'Well? From this story you can surely understand how precious books are!' Though he kept saying to me, 'Well? Now you understand, don't you?' as for me, where the preciousness lay, well, I still could not see it at all." The master's wife thus set forth her own view of the matter and pressed Meitei for an answer. Even the usually eloquent Meitei seemed somewhat at a loss this time; he drew a handkerchief from his sleeve, amused me with it for a while, and then, as if something had suddenly occurred to him, said in a loud voice, "But, madam, because Kushami buys so many books and stuffs his head with them at random, people call him a scholar or something of the sort. The other day I was looking through a certain literary magazine, and it had a notice of Kushami's writing." "Really?" The master's wife at once became serious. The moment a review of her own husband was mentioned, her interest was aroused; after all, husband and wife are husband and wife. She asked, "What did it say?" "Oh, nothing much, only two or three lines. It said that Kushami's prose is like drifting clouds and flowing water." The master's wife asked with a slight smile, "Was that all?" Meitei said, "Then it went on: 'When one thinks it has appeared, it vanishes at once; having gone, it long forgets to return.'" A puzzled expression came over the master's wife's face, and she said, "Is that praise?" Her tone sounded far from confident. Meitei answered unconcernedly, "Well, I should say it is praise, more or less." As he spoke, he again dangled the handkerchief before my eyes to tease me. The master's wife said, "Books may be the tools of his trade, so I suppose it cannot be helped, but he is really altogether too eccentric." Meitei thought to himself that the mistress was now circling in from another direction. He said, "Eccentric he is, to be sure, but people who pursue learning are always like that." Whether he was agreeing with the master's wife or defending the master was hard to tell. In any case, it was a clever answer that kept just the proper distance from both sides. The master's wife continued, "Take the other day, for example. He came home from school and had to go out somewhere at once, but changing clothes was too much trouble for him; what do you suppose he did? Without even taking off his overcoat, he sat on the desk and ate his meal, putting the dishes on the kotatsu frame. I sat beside him guarding the rice tub and watched him eat; it was so absurd I could hardly keep from laughing..." "It sounds like a modern-style inspection of a severed head. Still, that is precisely what makes Kushami Kushami. In short, he is anything but commonplace." Meitei thus forced himself to defend the master. The master's wife said, "We women do not understand this business of being commonplace or not commonplace; whatever you call it, it is far too outrageous."

paragraphs.source_zh: 那个皇帝还是有些不死心，又问她三册卖多少钱，据说那女人还是要九册的价钱。九册变成了六册，六册变成了三册，可价钱还和原来一样，一分钱也不肯让。假如还叫她让价，说不定还会把剩下的三册也投进火里去，这个皇帝终于付出高价把烧剩下的三册买了下来。我丈夫对我说：‘怎么样，通过这个故事你总可以明白书籍的可贵了吧！’尽管他一再向我说‘怎么样？这下可明白了吧，’可对于我，究竟可贵在哪里，唉，我还是不明白呀。”主人的妻子发表了自己的一套看法来催促迷亭的回答。看来，一向能说会道的迷亭，这回也有些难于作答了，便从袖里掏出一条手帕，逗弄我玩了一会儿，然后好像忽然想到什么，大声地说：“太太，苦沙弥那么喜欢买书，胡乱填满脑袋，别人会说他是学者啦或什么的呀。最近我翻了某一文学杂志，登出了评论苦沙弥的文章哩。”“真的？”主人的妻子立刻认真起来，一提出评论自己的丈夫，立刻唤起她的关心，看来夫妻毕竟还是夫妻。她问道：“上边都说些什么？”“也没什么，只是写了两三行罢了，说苦沙弥的文章宛如行云流水。”主人的妻子笑眯眯地问道：“就这些？”迷亭说：“下文嘛，还说：‘端倪乍露，立即无踪，逝而久久忘归。’”主人妻子的脸上现出迷惘的表情，说道：“这是夸奖的话吗？”她的语调似乎缺少信心。迷亭若无其事地回答说：“唔，应该说是夸奖的吧。”说着，又把手帕拎到我的眼前来逗弄我。主人的妻子说：“书籍是吃饭的本钱，又有什么办法，不过未免有点古怪得过分啦。”迷亭心想女主人又从另外的一方面来兜圈子啦。他说：“古怪是古怪，不过搞学问的人，总是要那样的。”也不知他是顺着主人的妻子说，还是替主人辩护。总之，是做了个不即不离的妙答。主人的妻子接着说：“就拿前些天来说，他从学校回来，马上要到别的地方去，他嫌换衣服麻烦，你猜怎么着？他连外套也不脱，坐在书桌上吃饭，把菜碟子放在熏笼上——我坐在旁边守着饭柜看着他吃，真是笑死人啦……”“倒像是现代化的‘验看首级’哩。不过，这种地方正是苦沙弥之所以为苦沙弥之处——总之是不落俗套啊。”迷亭硬着头皮替主人辩护。主人的妻子说：“我们做女人的，不懂得什么落俗套不落俗套，不管怎么说，太不像样啦。”
